correctness.rationale: For the canonical exchange-sign integral local system on the unordered complement of the diagonal, a finite equivariant relative CW decomposition gives free off-diagonal cells with the signed quotient differential. Diagonal pair homotopy reduction to a rose of cycle rank b yields C1=Z^b, C2=Z^{b(b+1)/2}, and zero integral differential. Signed transfer maps top cells to diagonal and symmetrized cross tensors, an integral basis for (V tensor V)^flip; degree-one transfer maps generators to twice a basis of H1 of the ordered relative pair and normalizes integrally. Naturality for automorphisms follows because transfer commutes with graph homeomorphisms. The exact standard-library program checks 109 cellular models, boundary-square zero, Q and F2 homology; experiments corroborate but do not prove the general result.

value.rationale: The coefficient system is not an arbitrary tweak: the exchange-sign character is canonically induced by forgetting labels of two particles. With constant coefficients, the known degree-one BM group is finite 2-torsion; with exchange-sign it becomes the full integral cycle lattice. The top group is naturally the divided square, retaining integral graph-symmetry information that disappears in Betti counts and differs from the ordinary symmetric coinvariant lattice at 2. This answers a motivated local-coefficient/symmetry question for every connected graph, not a numerical case or routine relabeling. The trace identity computes graph-symmetry characters without enumerating configuration cells. The contribution is restricted to two particles and this canonical system.
